credits.title: Credits
paragraphs: This card game originally came from a joke by Andrei Bituleanu, made for fun. I have no intention of selling it, since generative AI was used to apply filters to and regenerate real photographs of the game’s characters.

It would be my pleasure if any artist wished to redesign the AI-generated images with their own hand-drawn artwork, especially the Full Arts. They would receive the proper credit and thanks for their contribution.

I do not have the budget to hire artists because this site is non-profit. This is why the project is limited to my Echoes universe and is not an entity of my studio, Fracture Interactive, which has a zero-AI policy for every creative aspect of its products.

All of the game design, gameplay mechanics, rules, different cards, characters, and script was built entirely by hand. AI was only used for mathematical formulas for balancing during playtesting and for quickly translating the content into the other language.

AI also made it possible to code the technical infrastructure more quickly. The site’s frontend appearance was created through a hybrid process, with the creative UI/UX direction, like the color hue, the overall approach, the animations, the font-family and more coming from me. Although, AI has helped me build this infrastructure much faster.

Because AI was used extensively, and because I do not take this project side quest seriously, I do not intend to take it beyond a simple free game that explores my ideas and thoughts on a new kind of card game.
credits.note: If you appear among the Persona cards and ultimately wish to be removed from this game, you have the right to do so at any time. Simply contact me here so I can remove your card.

cards.title: Persona cards
paragraphs: Persona cards represent the characters you control, such as Andrei, Samuel, Paul, Oscar, etc.

points.text: is the resource used to activate abilities.
are unique to each Persona and may cost Tweak.
is a powerful action that makes the Persona Inert after use.

callout.title: Inert state
callout.text: An Inert Persona permanently loses access to all abilities. It remains on the field, keeps its remaining HP, and may still take damage. It becomes an HP reserve and continues producing Tweak for the duo until eliminated.

cards.title: Object cards
paragraphs: Objects, also called Items, improve the performance of your duo. They may reinforce abilities or support a particular strategy.
Each player has 3 Object slots in a best of three match.

cards.title: Reaction cards
paragraphs: Reactions are passive or situational effects obtained during the game. They may be used immediately after drawing or kept face down in the Reaction bank until their condition or effect prompts their use during either player's turn.
Each player has a maximum of 2 Reaction slots.
cards.note: A stored Reaction may be activated whenever its condition or effect prompts it, during the opponent's turn or during your own turn. Only one Reaction may be used during each opposing turn.

duoBuilding.title: Duo building
duoBuilding.intro: Two main strategies can be used to construct a duo.

strategies.label: Synergistic duo
strategies.title: Synergy
strategies.text: Pair two Personas whose abilities work effectively together. Use the three Object slots to strengthen their respective advantages. Both Personas collaborate to form a balanced unit and maximize their shared efficiency.

strategies.label: Antagonistic duo
strategies.title: Carry and Support
strategies.text: Pair Personas whose effects oppose one another. The Persona weakened by the interaction becomes the Support. The other becomes the Carry. The Carry deals most of the damage while the Support reinforces and maintains the strategy.

phases.title: Actions
phases.text: The active player may spend accumulated Tweak to:
items: Activate Persona abilities.
Use Objects.
Perform actions allowed by controlled cards.

phases.title: Tweak recovery
phases.text: At the start of the turn, the player gains Tweak equal to the combined Tweak of both Personas.

phases.title: Draw Reactions
phases.text: The player normally draws 1 Reaction at the end of the turn. It may be used immediately or placed face down in an available Reaction slot.
phases.note: If the player uses no abilities during the turn, they draw 2 Reaction cards instead of 1.

uses.label: Immediate
uses.text: When a Reaction is drawn, the player may activate it immediately.

uses.label: Prompted use
uses.text: A Reaction kept in the bank may be activated whenever its condition or effect prompts its use, during the opponent's turn or during your own turn.

entries.definition: A resource comparable to mana in other card games, required to use certain abilities.
A Persona state that prevents all ability use while preserving remaining HP.
A playable character with HP, Tweak, and unique abilities.
The main Persona in a duo, responsible for most of its damage.
A Persona focused on reinforcing or assisting a partner.
A card used immediately after drawing or whenever its condition or effect prompts its use during either player's turn.
A best of three match format.
A die with six faces numbered from 1 to 6. A notation such as 3 D6 means rolling three six-sided dice and adding their results unless stated otherwise.

object.name: Tenacity
object.description: When a card suffers lethal damage, it stays at 1 HP instead of dying. Single use.

reaction.name: Cig
reaction.description: Spend 1 Tweak to heal a card for 20 HP.

synergies.label: Natural combination
synergies.title: Synergistic duo
synergies.description: Both Personas directly reinforce their strengths and build a shared game plan.

synergies.label: Controlled risk
synergies.title: Antagonistic duo
synergies.description: One Persona exploits or endangers their partner. The Carry concentrates the power while the Support absorbs the cost.

blocks.text: Whenever Andrei is hit by an attack, he reflects 20% of the damage taken back to the attacker.
Andrei flips a coin to determine his target:

items: Heads: left opposing Persona.
Tails: right opposing Persona.

blocks.text: Deals 25 damage, plus 10 additional damage for each Choice card in the discard pile.
Andrei rolls 2d6 and gains Tweak equal to the sum for the current turn.
He then targets an opposing Persona and deals damage equal to 10 times the sum rolled.

blocks.label: At 100 HP or less
blocks.text: Roll 3d6 instead.
Andrei unleashes all his creativity to write psychologically unbearable horrors.
Every card on the field except Andrei takes 30 damage.
After damage is applied, any card, including Andrei, with 50 HP or less is instantly eliminated.
Time then stops for everyone except Andrei. Every other card, including his ally, suffers STUN for 1 turn.
Paul loves cigs. At the start of each of his turns, he restores 15 HP.
Deals 15 damage to both opposing Personas. He then draws a Reaction from the opponent's deck and discards it without using it.
Paul draws attention to himself and gains Tunnel. During the opponent's next turn, the enemy must target Paul with their attacks. Each use increases this ability's cost by 1 Tweak.
Paul smokes his best cigarette.
Restores 100% of his HP and draws 2 Reaction cards, which he plays immediately.
This Ultimate may be used as a Reaction when Paul dies.
When Samuel is eliminated, roll 1d6 at the start of the next turn:

items: 1-3: No effect.
4: Returns to life with 1 HP.
5: Returns to life with 100 HP.
6: Returns to life with 200 HP.

blocks.text: Samuel deals 5 damage to a Persona of his choice.
Each use increases this ability's damage by an additional 5.
Samuel chugs his beer and throws it, dealing 20 damage to an opposing Persona of his choice.
He may then choose to flip a coin once:

items: Heads: Deals 40 additional damage to the target.
Tails: Samuel takes 20 damage.

blocks.text: The coin flip is optional.
Samuel pops his best mush.
For this turn, all his abilities cost 0 Tweak.

blocks.label: Math Adept
blocks.text: May be used without limit. After the first use, Samuel takes damage equal to double the damage dealt to his target.

blocks.label: Cheers!
blocks.text: Samuel may flip the coin as many times as he wants until he gets Tails. Each Heads deals 20 additional damage. The first Tails deals 20 damage to Samuel and ends the flips.
Sam can roll to try to come back to life immediately after dying while on his ultimate.
Once per game, Oscar may activate this Passive as a Reaction to an attack or ability that hits him. He completely negates that attack or ability's damage.
Oscar chooses one of two effects:

items: Option 1: Deal 10 damage to every card on the field, including himself and his ally.
Option 2: Oscar and his ally each restore 10 HP.

blocks.text: Oscar performs a bunny hop on a Persona of his choice, dealing 50 damage.
Oscar leaves on a journey.
If his ally is Inert, they immediately become Active again and regain access to all abilities.
Because he lacks social cues, Jad is immune to every effect from Reaction cards.
Jad wants to fit in, so he imitates others.
Jad may copy and use any ability from a Persona currently in play.
The copied ability costs 1 additional Tweak.

blocks.label: Final cost
blocks.text: Original cost +1 Tweak.
Jad vapes so much that everyone completely forgets about him. He cannot be targeted for 1 turn.
Jad ruins all the effort he put into his glow-up.

blocks.label: Ally
blocks.text: Deals 60 damage to his own partner.

blocks.label: Opponents
blocks.text: Both opposing Personas are stunned for 2 turns.

blocks.label: Special interaction
blocks.text: If Xi is in the game, she is instantly eliminated.
Marion gives her team a fourth Object slot in its deck instead of the usual three.
Marion deals 10 damage to a target.
Whenever any card dies on the field, Rant’s damage is permanently doubled: 10, 20, 40, 80, and so on.
Rant always costs 2 Tweak.
Marion initially generates 0 Tweak per turn. Whenever a card dies on the field, her Tweak generation permanently increases by 1.
Marion chooses an opposing Persona and removes one of their abilities or their Passive. In exchange, Marion is stunned for 1 turn.
Marion unleashes all her negativity in an unbearable rant.
Every opposing card on the field, takes psychic damage equal to 10 + 50% of its remaining HP.
Marion is unaffected.
Whenever Xi takes damage, she gains 1 Tweak.
If the damage comes from Andrei, she gains 2 Tweak instead.
Xi deals 10 damage.
Xi rolls 4d6 and deals a burst of damage equal to the sum of the four dice.
She then restores HP equal to the damage dealt.

blocks.label: Damage and healing
blocks.text: 4 to 24 HP.
Xi has a credit bank starting at 10 credits.
At the start of each of her turns, she accumulates 10 additional credits.
When she activates her Ultimate, Xi spends all her credits and may distribute them freely between:
items: Damage: 1 credit for 1 damage.
Healing: 1 credit for 1 HP restored.

blocks.label: Special interaction
blocks.text: If Xi is eliminated by Jad's Grape Ultimate, she may still activate SOCIAL CREDIT as a Reaction and spend her accumulated credits.
Yan unlocks a third Reaction slot for his team instead of the usual two.
Yan deals damage equal to 50% of his missing HP.

blocks.label: Example
blocks.text: At 100 HP out of 220, he is missing 120 HP and therefore deals 60 damage.

items: Yan deals 20 damage to both opposing Personas.
OR: Yan deals 30 damage to a Persona of his choice.

blocks.text: He then gains Tunnel.
Yan sacrifices every Object owned by his team.
In exchange, he resurrects his ally with 100% of their HP.

When Jesus is below half HP, he may sacrifice up to 30 HP to increase the damage of Gambling's Power at a 1:1 ratio: each HP sacrificed adds 1 damage, for a maximum of +30 damage. The amount must be chosen before rolling.
Jesus rolls 1d6 to determine his target:

items: 1-2: Deals 35 damage to his ally if they are still alive.
3-4: Deals 35 damage to the left opposing Persona.
5-6: Deals 35 damage to the right opposing Persona.

blocks.text: Jesus deals 20 damage to himself and destroys 1 opposing Object.
For the next 5 turns, Jesus has a 50% chance each turn to be immune to all damage.
In addition, when he rolls a 6 for Gambling's Power, he chooses his target and deals 70 damage instead.
You cannot use Reactions while Gabriel is alive. You consume them through 3D Eye.
Gabriel slashes with his pen, dealing 20 damage to the card on his left.
He deals damage equal to 5 times the number of Eyes he currently holds to the card on his right.
Gabriel draws a Reaction, then sends it to the discard pile without using it.
He gains Eyes equal to the card's rarity: 1 for Common, 2 for Rare, 3 for Epic, and 5 for Legendary.
Gabriel redraws the rules.
Gabriel may replace any card's Passive, ability, or Ultimate with a Passive, ability, or Ultimate from any other card on the field, excluding himself.
After using 4D Artist, the directions of 2D Art are reversed: it deals 20 damage to the card on Gabriel’s right and damage equal to 5 times his Eyes to the card on his left.
Gabriel does not become Inert after using this ability.
When Jake reaches 100 HP or less, he only takes 50% of incoming damage.
Jake stabs 6 times in a row. Roll 6d6; the sum of all rolls is the damage dealt to his chosen target.
Jake applies Tunnel to himself. Until the next turn, he reflects 100% of the damage dealt to him equally to its source.
Jake writes horrors about a Persona of his choice. He chooses one of two damage options: deal a flat 75 damage, or roll 15d6 + 30 and deal the resulting total.
Victor’s attacks apply Burns. Each Burn deals 5 damage per turn for 2 turns.
Victor deals 15 damage to a card of his choice and applies 3 Burns to it.
Victor sets every opposing card ablaze, dealing 3d6 damage and applying 2 Burns to each of them.
Victor incinerates the field and burns all of his Objects.
Each opposing Persona and Victor’s ally take 30 fire damage, plus 10 damage for each active Burn on that card.
All Burns are then removed from every card.
If at least one card dies in the fire, Victor does not become Inert.

personas.ultimateAftermath: VICTOR BECOMES INERT UNLESS AT LEAST ONE CARD DIES IN THE FIRE

blocks.text: At the start of each turn, Kenny has a 33% chance to reflect 100% of the damage he takes from abilities during that turn. The opposing team doesn't know when this effect is active.
Kenny fires a shotgun at his target, dealing 40 damage and taking 10 damage himself.
Kenny chooses the first ability of any Persona in the match and uses it on a Persona of his choice.
Kenny curses the opposing team. During that turn, each opposing Persona takes 50 damage plus additional damage equal to 20% of Kenny’s missing HP.
He may also use any active effect from the opponents’ Objects.
Tom is not afraid of danger. The first time he reaches 50% HP or less, the cost of all his abilities is permanently reduced by 1 Tweak for the rest of the match.
Tom slashes both opposing Personas with his katana, dealing 35 damage to each of them.
Each target is checked independently and has a 25% chance to receive a critical hit for double damage instead.
Tom increases the Tweak cost of one opposing ability by 1.
Tom dashes through both opposing Personas with his katana, dealing 40 damage to each of them. The entire dash makes one 25% critical-hit check; on a critical hit, both targets take 80 damage instead.
Tom increases the Tweak cost of every ability belonging to both opposing Personas by 2.
He also reduces the Tweak cost of every ability belonging to his ally by 1. This reduction cannot lower an ability’s cost below 1 Tweak.
After the first attack that hits Charbel during a turn, he becomes immune to every subsequent attack for the remainder of that turn.
Charbel inspires himself and his ally. Both gain a 20% damage boost for the remainder of the turn.
Roll 2d6. Charbel chooses one die and deals damage equal to 10 times its result to a target of his choice. He then takes damage equal to 10 times the other die’s result.
Charbel unleashes Chaos against all odds.
Every card on the field loses all of its Objects and Reactions.
Each opposing Persona rolls 2d6 and takes damage equal to 20 times its highest result.
Charbel and his ally each roll 2d6 and take damage equal to 20 times their lowest result.
Seb begins the match with a 5% chance for his abilities to critically hit.
His critical-hit chance permanently increases by 1 percentage point at the start of each turn and by 1 percentage point every time he is hit.
Seb chooses one of two attack patterns:

items: Concentrated strike: deal 2x20 damage to one target.
Split strike: deal 20 damage to each opposing Persona.

blocks.text: Seb performs an X-shaped slash on an opposing Persona of his choice, dealing 50 damage and marking them.
Until the end of Seb’s next turn, he deals 50% more damage to the marked target.
When Seb takes damage that would eliminate him, he enters Last Stand and immediately ends the opponent’s current turn.
His current critical-hit chance and all damage he deals are doubled. His critical-hit chance cannot exceed 100%.
Seb performs Double Katana and Samurai Slash one final time before dying.

personas.ultimateAftermath: SEB DIES AFTER HIS LAST STAND

blocks.text: Whenever Fred attacks, he has a 50% chance to regain all the Tweak spent on that ability.
Fred can spend 1 Tweak to deal 4d6 damage. Each additional Tweak spent adds 2d6 damage to the attack.
He then attacks one random Persona from the opposing duo.
Fred deals between 1 and 90 damage to a target of his choice.
Fred grants his ally a 25% chance to reset their abilities after use.
Fred also begins a potential succession of area attacks against the opposing duo. Each attack deals 6d6 damage and has a 75% chance to reset.
